title: Early nationalism & the INC
examples: What was the main difference between the Moderates and the Extremists?
Can you explain the methods used by the early nationalists?
Who were the key leaders associated with these groups?

explain.say: Today we look at early Indian nationalism groups. We will compare two main groups. These groups were the Moderates and the Extremists.
The Moderates believed in polite requests to the British. They wanted reforms through established laws. They believed in working within the British system.
The Extremists felt polite requests were not enough. They demanded immediate and sweeping changes. They believed in self-reliance and strong action.
A concrete example of Moderates was the early use of the Indian Councils Act. They sought minor administrative changes through these councils. This showed their patience.
An example of Extremist action was the Swadeshi movement. People boycotted foreign goods and promoted local Indian products. This was a powerful economic tool.

In everyday life, when a community needs a better park, they might first write polite letters to the council. If that fails, they might organize a large public protest. This shows the shift in methods.

faq.q: What was the main difference between the two groups?
faq.a: The Moderates preferred peaceful, constitutional methods like petitions. The Extremists favoured more direct action like boycotts.

faq.q: Did the Moderates ever suggest violence?
faq.a: No, the Moderates strictly believed in working within the existing legal framework. They avoided confrontation at all costs.

faq.q: What does Swadeshi mean in this context?
faq.a: Swadeshi means promoting goods made in one's own country. It was an economic boycott against foreign goods.
asks: What was the goal of Swadeshi?

faq.q: Were the leaders the same for both groups?
faq.a: While there was overlap, the leaders often represented different levels of commitment to change. Some leaders shifted their views over time.
The Extremists adopted more radical measures that challenged the ruling authority directly. The Moderates were more cautious in their approach.

facts: The Moderates believed in gradual political reform within the British system.
The Extremists believed that self-rule could only be achieved through mass action.
Swadeshi was an economic movement promoting indigenous Indian goods.
The early Congress saw a shift in tactics from petitioning to direct action.

quiz.say: Boycotting foreign cloth shows the idea of:
quiz.why: Swadeshi was the specific movement focused on promoting local Indian products.

wrong.1: Non-cooperation is a broader action, while Swadeshi is about goods.
wrong.2: Petitioning is a request, not an economic boycott.
wrong.3: Reform is the goal, but Swadeshi is the method used.

quiz.say: If a group believes only in working within the law, they are most like:
quiz.why: Moderates were defined by their faith in working within the established legal and political structures.

wrong.0: Reformers is too general; Moderates is the historical term.
wrong.2: Extremists believed the law needed to be fundamentally challenged.
wrong.3: Protesters can be any group, not specific to the early INC.
